key_insight: Among the tested detonation-sprayed WC coatings, the Co–Cr binder delivered the best combined hardness, friction, scratch resistance, and corrosion performance.
engineering_relevance: WC–Co–Cr coatings are promising for pipeline valves and other oil-and-gas components exposed to wear and corrosive environments.
method: Compared detonation-sprayed WC coatings with Co–Cr, Ni, and NiCr binders.
Characterized microstructure and elemental distribution using SEM and EDS mapping.
Evaluated microhardness, tribology, scratch resistance, and electrochemical corrosion.
evidence_signal: WC–Co–Cr reached 1232.55 HV and a friction coefficient of 0.515, while porosity was lowest for WC–Ni (0.40%) and highest for WC–NiCr (2.78%); corrosion testing used 3.5 wt.% NaCl.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish long-term field durability under combined wear and corrosion, so service-specific validation remains necessary.
paper_title: Impact Of Co–Cr, Ni, and NiCr binder systems on the microstructure and functional properties of WC coatings produced by detonation spraying
